items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Her daddy would have known, though. [INTERVIEWEE] Your father would have known.

ctx.x: And, you know, as we were saying, Ted, we were talking about writing columns and so forth, about knowing people, about getting involved, having the right kind of connection, so that you could get into the structure of putting something together to inform in a newspaper, because a lot of people call newspaper an organ. It's an organ of information. That's what a newspaper is. See, and I highlight, I was talking about Charlie Rosenthal over in Orange, Texas, who was a good friend of Frank Pannier. Both of them were…
Her daddy would have known, though.

Your father would have known. And so, from Lake Charles, we went to Opelousas and to many other people, because, like I said, they had a lot of friends over there, like Ike Williamson, and then I had Tooney Forkard, who was a big-time gambler, who had a club in Lake Charles called The Arrow. Now, he promoted a lot of shows in the Lake Charles area, because, you see, I think I mentioned about the Army Air Force Base there in Lake Charles during World War II, and that had growth, given growth to Lake Charles,…
